text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Denmark receives support from UNESCO, the United Nations education body, to host an academy for the teaching and study of democracy. Minister of education Ole Vig Jensen says the academy could go into operation in a year's time.
--Danish consumers have become better at running their economy, assessing the need for purchases and the state of their economy before consumption, unlike the reckless 1980s, a new report shows.
--Danish banks are organising more and more loans for industry, while mortgage credit forms are helping an ever growing number of private citizens with house and other loans.
--The weaker Danish crown currency is helping Denmark's exports to revive and export industries to recover lost market shares abroad.

--Smaller Danish shipping lines are being hit by lower cargo rates, with some container rates more than 25 percent down within the past year. Only major Danish shipper A.P. Moeller is benefiting from the lower rates, which are expected to go on falling in the coming months.
--Denmark's A.P. Moeller group is a member of an international consortium which has reached the last round of tendering for a contract to operate the container port in Montevideo. Uruguay.
--The new strong British pound and Swedish crown has helped Danish exports to two of Denmark's most important trading partners to boom, with firms in all sectors reporting improved sales.
--If share prices at Copenhagen stock exchange hold present levels for the rest of 1997, bank paper can expect an overall gain of eight billion crowns in value.
